subdomain: 3.1 Evaluate tool/agent configuration for capability bloat

en.question: A factory agent diagnoses equipment faults and schedules inspections. A shared integration template also exposes a tool that changes robot safety interlocks, although this role is never authorized to change them. Which configuration change best addresses this capability bloat?

options.text: Keep the interlock tool but require the agent to explain its reason before calling it.
options.note: An explanation is model-generated behavior, not a permission boundary. The agent would retain a capability outside its authorized role.

options.text: Remove the interlock tool from this role and deny interlock changes in its backend permissions.
options.note: Removing the callable capability and its underlying permission aligns both interfaces with the role. A discovered or accidentally constructed call cannot regain the prohibited operation.

options.text: Defer the interlock tool until tool search finds it, leaving its credentials unchanged.
options.note: Deferred loading reduces initial definition context but leaves the tool discoverable and executable. It does not remove the unauthorized capability.

options.text: Keep the shared template and alert an operator after any interlock change.
options.note: Post-action monitoring can detect misuse but cannot prevent a safety setting from changing. The role does not need this capability in the first place.
